name: Kitten Care Checklist
description: A kitten care checklist covering the day-to-day routine of feeding, litter, play, grooming, and health for a kitten.

items.text: Feed small, frequent meals of age-appropriate kitten food.
Provide clean, fresh water and encourage drinking.
Wash bowls daily to keep them clean.
Stick to vet-recommended food and limit treats.
Adjust meal frequency as your kitten grows.
items.note: Confirm the schedule with your veterinarian.

items.text: Note any loss of appetite to mention to the vet.
Scoop the litter box at least once a day.
Use a low-sided box and kitten-safe litter.
Fully change the litter and clean the box regularly.
Keep the box quiet, accessible, and away from food.
Gently guide your kitten to the box after meals and naps.
Watch for changes in litter use to share with your vet.
Schedule several short, interactive play sessions daily.
Use wand toys and balls to channel hunting energy.
Redirect biting and scratching from hands to toys.
Provide a scratching post and safe climbing spots.
Spend calm cuddle time to build trust.
Rotate toys to keep your kitten curious.
Brush the coat gently and regularly to reduce hairballs.
Introduce nail trims slowly and positively.
Handle paws, ears, and mouth to prepare for future care.
Check eyes and ears and clean gently if needed.
Start gentle dental care as your vet advises.
Keep grooming sessions short and rewarding.
Keep cords, small items, and toxic plants out of reach.
Supervise young children and teach gentle handling.
Check appliances and recliners before use.
Secure windows, balconies, and doors against escapes.
Provide a warm, quiet place to nap undisturbed.
Keep a secure carrier ready for vet trips.
Watch appetite, energy, weight, and litter habits daily.
Keep up with the vaccination and deworming schedule.
Give any prescribed medications exactly as directed.
Check skin and coat for fleas and irritation.
Keep your kitten warm, hydrated, and rested.
Important: This is general information, not veterinary advice. Always consult a veterinarian about your kitten's health, diet, and vaccinations.

faq.q: How often should I feed a kitten?
faq.a: Young kittens usually eat small meals several times a day, with frequency decreasing as they grow. Feed an age-appropriate kitten food and provide fresh water. Your veterinarian can confirm the right schedule and portions for your kitten's age and weight.

faq.q: How do I keep a kitten's litter box clean?
faq.a: Scoop the litter box at least once a day, fully change the litter regularly, and use a low-sided box a kitten can enter easily. A clean, accessible box supports good habits and lets you spot any change worth mentioning to your vet.

faq.q: How much should I play with my kitten?
faq.a: Aim for several short, interactive play sessions a day to burn energy, build coordination, and strengthen your bond. Use wand toys and balls, redirect biting from hands to toys, and provide a scratching post and safe enrichment between sessions.

faq.q: How is this different from the kitten checklist?
faq.a: This kitten care checklist focuses on the daily routine of feeding, litter, play, and health. Our broader Kitten Checklist tracks first-year milestones like vaccinations, growth, and development.

faq.q: Can I download this kitten care checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print it for the kitchen or download it as a PDF so the whole family can follow the same daily kitten routine.
